searches.reason: Move beyond shuffle sensitivity to locate where GRU4Rec loses useful history information. Seek bounded probes linking lag-specific gradients and controlled hidden-state interventions to target–competitor margins, with finite-difference checks and zero-intervention controls. Distinguish recurrent forgetting from output-score insensitivity; neither establishes current intent or generalization.

searches.reason: Connect diagnosis to reported failures using item titles, descriptions and explicit feedback from the twenty simulator users. Seek evidence-grounded annotation protocols separating broad association, documented compatibility, redundancy and insufficient information. Require quoted evidence, abstention and agreement checks; missing specifications must not become inferred incompatibility, mood or dislike. Keep results descriptive given five users per category.
searches.query: recommendation explanation evaluation evidence grounded user feedback taxonomy compatibility redundancy insufficient information annotation abstention inter annotator agreement 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Challenge whether strong sampled training margins identify meaningful ranking quality, particularly for low-frequency Electronics items. Seek candidate-set stress tests comparing frozen uniform negatives with training-frequency-matched and title-similar distractors, plus chunked full-catalog scoring by the same checkpoint. Measure failure overlap and sensitivity to candidate construction without changing the host benchmark or treating training-prefix results as held-out performance.
